To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel, efficient method for on-line, kernel-based density estimation, and we show that it can be used for prior learning and context-based active localization of objects in visual situations.

(1) a flexible, kernel-based model of the expected spatial structure can be learned from training images, (2) the system can actively localize objects in new images by exploiting the context discovered in the image, and (3) this process can be performed efficiently, even for large training sets, by using an on-line, multipole expansion technique.

(1) a novel on-line kernel density estimator based on multipole expansions can be used to update probabilistic models of visual scenes, and (2) these models can be used to improve the performance of active object localization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a general framework for active object localization in visual scenes, based on a flexible, kernel-based representation of situation knowledge.
the following question: how can we build and use flexible models of visual situations to facilitate efficient object localization in images?
a fundamental question: How can we enable computers to understand the visual world?

the method proposed in this paper is a very promising approach for the task of object localization in images.

our system is capable of learning and localizing objects in a given situation, and is able to do so in an efficient, scalable manner.

we propose a novel algorithm for fast on-line kernel density estimate and use it to localize a target object in images.
our method is a general approach for learning interpretable probabilistic models for a given task and using them in an active search for relevant objects.
we have shown that the use of context in the learning process can be very beneficial for object localization in visual scenes.

, given a small amount of prior knowledge, a computer can learn to recognize and localize visual situations.
a small number of training images, together with an efficient kernel density estimation algorithm, can support highly accurate object localization in visual scenes.
the ability to dynamically generate interpretable, probabilistically-based, and context-sensitive models can support a new generation of vision systems that can learn to recognize complex situations.
